artists.biography: Electronic were an alternative dance supergroup formed by New Order singer and guitarist Bernard Sumner and ex-Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr. They co-wrote the majority of their output between 1989 and 1998, collaborating with Neil Tennant and Chris Lowe, of the Pet Shop Boys, on three tracks in their early years, and former Kraftwerk member Karl Bartos on nine songs in 1995.

perplexity.description:
Get The Message – The Best of Electronic is a greatest hits compilation album by Electronic, the English alternative dance supergroup formed by Bernard Sumner (New Order) and Johnny Marr (The Smiths). Released in 2006, the album spans recordings from 1989 to 1998 and showcases the band's fusion of electronic music, alternative rock, and pop. It includes most of their A-sides, select B-sides, and notable album tracks, highlighting their blend of synthesizers, guitars, and analogue technology that defined their sound.

This compilation captures Electronic's evolution from their debut single "Getting Away with It" (1989), which combined dance beats with rock elements and featured collaborations with Neil Tennant and Karl Bartos, through to later work that leaned more heavily into guitar-driven alternative rock and house influences. The album reflects their critical and commercial success, including hits like "Get the Message" and "Feel Every Beat," and serves as a comprehensive overview of their innovative approach to genre blending during the 1990s. Released by Warner Music and Parlophone, it consolidates Electronic’s legacy as pioneers of alternative dance and rock fusion.
